newsitem.title: USA: U.S. food aid to N. Korea to arrive in early May.
newsitem.headline: U.S. food aid to N. Korea to arrive in early May.

text.p: Two U.S. shipments of food aid to North Korea totalling 27,000 metric tons will arrive in the North Korean port of Nampo in the first half of May, the State Department said on Thursday.
Spokesman Nicholas Burns said the first ship, a U.S. flagged vessel, would arrive around May 4 and the second, bearing an unidentified foreign flag, around May 12.

The food -- bagged corn, rice and corn-soy blend -- is a $10 million U.S. contribution first announced on Feb. 19 to a World Food Programme appeal for aid to alleviate famine in North Korea caused partly by severe flooding.

The two ships would begin loading late in March, Burns said. On arrival in Nampo, near Pyongyang, the food would be unloaded by WFP staff who would distribute it to the needy, primarly malnourished children under five.
